title: Living in space
examples: How do astronauts eat their food up there?
Is it really hard to sleep in space?
What is the International Space Station like?

explain.say: Today we learn about living up in space.

items: It is the state of floating freely.

explain.say: In microgravity, things float all around you.
The International Space Station is a big home in space.
Astronauts eat special food that does not leak.
Sleeping in space needs special bags to stay put.
In real life, when you go on a roller coaster, you feel weightless for a moment.

faq.q: Do astronauts feel like they are floating all the time?
faq.a: Yes, they are constantly in a state of weightlessness. They might also ask, "Why do astronauts float?" or "What is weightlessness like?"
asks: How is it to float in space?

faq.q: Is the International Space Station very big?
faq.a: It is a very large structure built in orbit around Earth. You might also ask, "What is the ISS?" or "How big is the space station?"
asks: How big is the space station?

faq.q: How do they eat food in microgravity?
faq.a: Food is often dehydrated or sealed in pouches to prevent it from floating away. Other ways to ask this are, "What do astronauts eat?" or "How do they keep food down?"
asks: How do they keep food down?

faq.q: Do they have to sleep in special ways?
faq.a: Yes, they use straps or sleeping bags to anchor themselves to a wall. You could also ask, "How do astronauts sleep?" or "What do they use to sleep?"
asks: What do they use to sleep?

faq.a: Yes, everything that is not attached to something else will float. You might also ask, "Is there gravity in space?" or "What keeps things down?"

facts: Microgravity means the absence of weight.
The International Space Station orbits the Earth.
Astronauts must secure items to keep them from floating.
Food in space is often dehydrated or packaged.

quiz.say: If you are floating in microgravity, what happens to a loose pen?

options.show: It will float up to the ceiling.
options.say: It will float up to the ceiling.

options.show: It will float until it hits something.
options.say: It will float until it hits something.

options.show: It will fall to the floor.
options.say: It will fall to the floor.

options.show: It will stick to the nearest wall.
options.say: It will stick to the nearest wall.

quiz.why: In microgravity, there is no strong pull downwards, so the pen simply floats.

wrong.0: Floating is equally likely in all directions, not just up.
wrong.2: This assumes Earth's gravity is pulling it down constantly.
wrong.3: This suggests a magnetic force that is not present.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of the International Space Station?

options.show: To conduct scientific research in space.
options.say: To conduct scientific research in space.

options.show: To serve as a long-term human settlement.
options.say: To serve as a long-term human settlement.

options.show: To launch all future space missions.
options.say: To launch all future space missions.

options.show: To observe Earth's weather patterns only.
options.say: To observe Earth's weather patterns only.

quiz.why: The ISS is designed as a laboratory orbiting Earth for scientific study.

wrong.1: While it houses people, its primary function is research, not just living.
wrong.2: It is a station, not a primary launch platform.
wrong.3: Its research covers many scientific fields, not just weather.

quiz.say: When sleeping in space, what is necessary to prevent drifting?
quiz.why: You must physically tie yourself down to a surface to stay in one place.

wrong.0: There is no natural magnetic field strong enough for this purpose.
wrong.1: Such a suit is not required for basic sleeping.
wrong.2: Without restraints, any small movement will cause you to drift away.
